content:
christine (sales): quick sync — customer wants inbound traffic to reach our Private deploy in their VPC but fronted by their edge (they'll BYOIP / hand us an EIP). they need client source IP preserved for auth logs and WAF rules. can we support this in the POC?
omar_se: short answer: yes, but topology matters. need to confirm whether the customer expects traffic to terminate at their proxy then forward to our VPC, or if they want our endpoint to be publicly reachable from their EIP. both have different constraints.
customer-netops: flow we want: internet -> customer edge (BYOIP EIP) -> internal reverse proxy -> route to redwood private endpoint in our VPC via TGW/VPC peering. preserve client IP end-to-end if possible. mutual TLS for auth.
netops_jake: important bits:
- if traffic goes through customer's reverse proxy and then to us over peering/TGW, source IP will be the proxy's IP unless they use proxy-protocol or X-Forwarded-For.
- NLB preserves client source IP for TCP, ALB does not (it SNATs).
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is consumer-initiated outbound from customer to our service; it doesn't give you a public BYOIP EIP in front.
- For static egress IP from customer-to-us you can use customer's NAT with EIP. inbound public EIP in front of their edge is fine but that doesn't magically preserve original public IP after proxy.
omar_se: recommendation for preserving client IP and keeping things simple for POC:
1) internet -> customer BYOIP EIP -> their reverse proxy (term TLS) -> forward to NLB in their VPC using proxy-protocol v2 (so we can see client IP) -> NLB -> connection across TGW/peering to our Private deploy (or directly to a dedicated ENI in their VPC if using Private deployment).
2) Or: if customer can open outbound to our PrivateLink endpoint, use PrivateLink; in that case we can't attach their BYOIP EIP to the path, but we still get a secure VPC-to-VPC fabric and you can include client IP in headers.
alice_security: security notes:
- mutual TLS is fine, need cert exchange plan.
- WAF rules based on X-Forwarded-For are OK but trust chain required (only the reverse proxy should inject XFF).
- firewall rules should lock to their edge proxy CIDRs + redwood control-plane ranges. we should NOT accept arbitrary source IPs.
ben_platform: small SG example for our side (customer will mirror rules):
```
# allow only customer's proxy IP range to reach app port
Type: custom TCP
Port: 443
Source: 203.0.113.0/28  # replace with customer's proxy eip range
```
customer-netops: a couple clarifications: can we use NLB with TLS terminate at the proxy, then TCP pass-through to NLB? we want to avoid double TLS if possible.
netops_jake: yes. options:
- TLS terminate at customer proxy, then proxy opens plain TCP to NLB: easier but you lose mTLS between proxy and app unless you re-establish.
- TCP passthrough all the way to our service: NLB in TCP mode, TLS terminates at our side; preserves client IP and TLS. drawback: can't inspect TLS at their proxy.
christine (sales): pricing question from customer: does using Private deploy + peering/TGW add incremental cost vs PrivateLink?
omar_se: Private deploy (VPC peering/TGW) — costs: egress across TGW/peering, any NAT/EIPs on their side, and our provisioning (private deployment license). PrivateLink — charges per endpoint hour and data processed; also requires our service to be exposed as an endpoint service. costs differ by traffic pattern; we can run a quick estimate if they give expected GB/month.
alice_security: compliance note: if customer requires no public internet ingress at all into their VPC, PrivateLink is preferable (consumer-only inbound to our service over interface endpoints). BYOIP/EIP implies public-facing edge, so that fails 'no public ingress' policy. confirm policy.
customer-netops: they will allow a public BYOIP EIP at their edge for the POC but prefer PrivateLink for production. ok.
deploy-bot: deployment started: private-deploy/2026-03-18T09:30Z -> staging (task 8421) :construction:
ben_platform: test checklist for POC (quick):
- 1) customer hands us the proxy egress CIDR and sample certs for mTLS.
- 2) customer spins up NLB in front of their proxy or configures proxy-protocol if using NLB.
- 3) we provision security groups and route towards customer's VPC peering/TGW attachment.
- 4) smoke test: curl from internet -> BYOIP -> proxy -> reach private deploy. example (from customer's edge):
```bash
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:203.0.113.10 https://api.redwood.internal/health 
# or to test client IP header
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.internal' --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:203.0.113.10 https://api.redwood.internal/echo-ip
```
omar_se: also run this to validate proxy-protocol when using NLB:
```bash
# use socat or h2load to send proxy-protocol v2 header if you need to test locally
```
christine (sales): next steps — can we get a short network-ops-only call with customer and our SE + netops to lock topology? availability weds 14:00 PT.
customer-netops: confirmed. we'll send EIP ranges and sample certs before the call.
omar_se: I'll prep a minimal architecture diagram + firewall rule snippet and a quick cost delta table for PrivateLink vs peering for ~5 TB/month and share ahead of the meeting.
alice_security: I'll include required audit/logging controls and what we need in the security questionnaire.
christine (sales): perfect — thanks team. action items: @omar_se prep diagram, @ben_platform prepare SG snippet, @alice_security security checklist. i'll cc customer and book the call. :thumbsup:
